record.context_brief: Finite order monodromy for isolated hypersurface singularities
record.original_question: For an isolated hypersurface singularity given locally by f(z1,...,z_{n+1})=s, with nonsingular Milnor fibers M_s over s in the punctured disc and Picard-Lefschetz transformation T acting on H^n(M_s0,Q), is T of finite order?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $U \subset \mathbb{C}^{n+1}$ be an open neighborhood of the origin and let $f : U \to \mathbb{C}$ be a holomorphic function with $f(0) = 0$ such that $0$ is an isolated critical point of $f$. For sufficiently small $\varepsilon > 0$ and $0 < \eta \ll \varepsilon$, set $B = \{z \in \mathbb{C}^{n+1} : \|z\| \le \varepsilon\}$ and let $D^* = \{s \in \mathbb{C} : 0 < |s| < \eta\}$. For $s \in D^*$ define the Milnor fiber
$$M_s = \{z \in B : f(z) = s\},$$
which is a smooth compact manifold with boundary, homotopy equivalent to a bouquet of $n$-spheres. Fix a base point $s_0 \in D^*$ and let $T : H^n(M_{s_0}, \mathbb{Q}) \to H^n(M_{s_0}, \mathbb{Q})$ be the Picard–Lefschetz monodromy transformation obtained by parallel-transporting cohomology classes once around the origin along the loop $s_0 e^{2\pi i t}$, $t \in [0,1]$.

Question: Is $T$ necessarily of finite order, i.e. does there exist a positive integer $N$ such that $T^N = \mathrm{id}$ on $H^n(M_{s_0}, \mathbb{Q})$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is resolved by the monodromy theorem (Brieskorn, "Die Monodromie der isolierten Singularitäten von Hyperflächen", 1970; also Landman, Clemens, Deligne, Grothendieck): for any isolated hypersurface singularity the Picard–Lefschetz monodromy $T$ acting on $H^n(M_{s_0}, \mathbb{Q})$ is quasi-unipotent — its eigenvalues are roots of unity and $(T^N - I)^{n+1} = 0$ for some positive integer $N$. Consequently $T$ is of finite order if and only if it is semisimple (equivalently, if and only if a resolution graph contains no cycles in the surface case); in general nontrivial Jordan blocks occur, so $T$ need not be of finite order. Thus the question is answered: $T$ is always quasi-unipotent but not always of finite order.

status_evidence.title: Die Monodromie der isolierten Singularitäten von Hyperflächen
status_evidence.snippet: Brieskorn's paper proving that the monodromy of an isolated hypersurface singularity is quasi-unipotent.
status_evidence.claim: The monodromy operator on the cohomology of the Milnor fiber of an isolated hypersurface singularity is quasi-unipotent (its eigenvalues are roots of unity).

status_evidence.title: Monodromy (Ebeling)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of monodromy of isolated hypersurface singularities, including the monodromy theorem and conditions for finite order.
status_evidence.claim: Monodromy is quasi-unipotent; finite-order monodromy corresponds to special cases such as resolution graphs without cycles.

status_evidence.title: Isolated Hypersurface Singularities (Griffiths, 2019)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of the monodromy theorem for isolated hypersurface singularities.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference confirming the monodromy theorem in the form stated by Brieskorn–Landman.
